claim_boundary.rule: Each entry is an explicit strongest-parent first-refusal record for one named #602 Section-Q tradition. A parent mechanism is adopted/subtracted at its stated scope before any GMI residual may be retained.

parents.name: Turing, On Computable Numbers, with an Application to the Entscheidungsproblem
parents.citation: Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society s2-42:230-265, 1937; DOI 10.1112/plms/s2-42.1.230

parents.name: Minsky, Computation: Finite and Infinite Machines
parents.citation: Prentice-Hall, 1967; machine/register-machine simulation and computability theory

entries.what_parent_explained: Universal-machine formalisms own computable representability and semantics-preserving simulation. They do not identify a resource-optimal morphology, learning law, acquisition path, phase boundary or developmental trajectory. A universal interpreter may simulate the same target with arbitrarily different charged overhead, so universality is a representability parent rather than a morphology-selection theorem.

disposition_detail.adopt: Use computability/universal simulation as the representability baseline and explicit UNIVERSAL_COMPUTATION_ONLY null.
disposition_detail.reject: Any claim that Turing universality alone predicts the selected intelligence morphology, learning law, search burden or developmental path.
disposition_detail.leave_open: Registered resource/development laws that distinguish universal realizations after simulation overhead, acquisition, verification and update cost are charged.

entries.prior_information_added: Classical computability and universal-machine simulation; #602 T602-03 supplies the explicit semantics-preserving overhead witness.
entries.higher_order_question_remaining: Which equivalence class of universal realizations is feasible, reachable and Pareto-undominated in a registered ecology?
entries.parent_sufficient_at_scope: PARENT_OWNED for computable representability and simulation; insufficient for GMI morphology/development prediction.

parents.name: Hutter, Universal Artificial Intelligence
parents.citation: Springer, 2005; Sequential Decisions Based on Algorithmic Probability; DOI 10.1007/b138233

parents.name: Legg and Hutter, Universal Intelligence: A Definition of Machine Intelligence

entries.what_parent_explained: AIXI/universal-agent theory already supplies idealized simplicity-weighted sequential decision objectives, while Legg-Hutter supplies a broad environment-weighted intelligence measure. Those objects are normative/universal-agent parents under their own reward, environment-class and computability assumptions; they do not by themselves provide a tractable morphology, learning or lifecycle phase law.

disposition_detail.adopt: Treat AIXI/universal-intelligence objectives and their assumptions as the first-refusal universal-agent baseline.
disposition_detail.adapt: Any computable GMI instantiation must expose approximation/search/resource assumptions and the frozen task/reward measure.
disposition_detail.reject: Relabeling a bounded GMI agent as a novel universal agent, or using an ideal universal objective as evidence of tractable morphology selection.
disposition_detail.leave_open: Resource-bounded, ecology-conditioned predictive laws over realizable morphologies after the normative environment/reward measure is fixed.

entries.prior_information_added: Algorithmic-information universal-agent theory and universal-intelligence measurement.
entries.higher_order_question_remaining: Can a registered finite/resource-bounded GMI law predict morphology and development beyond what the chosen universal-agent objective already specifies?
entries.parent_sufficient_at_scope: PARENT_OWNED for the universal-agent objective/measure at its stated idealized scope.

parents.name: Finn, Abbeel and Levine, Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning
Duan et al., RL^2: Fast Reinforcement Learning via Slow Reinforcement Learning
Wang et al., Learning to reinforcement learn

entries.what_parent_explained: Meta-learning already owns training parameters, recurrent dynamics or update procedures so that later tasks are learned faster. MAML optimizes for rapid few-step adaptation; RL^2 and related meta-RL embed a learned fast learning procedure in recurrent state. Therefore reduced future acquisition burden is not a GMI novelty merely because it is inherited across tasks.

disposition_detail.adopt: Use MAML/meta-RL/learned-optimizer systems as parents for faster future adaptation under matched task distributions.
disposition_detail.adapt: Charge meta-training, persistent state, reset, maintenance and harmful transfer, and distinguish warm-start replay from genuinely lower future search burden.
disposition_detail.reject: Calling any cross-task speedup 'evolvability' without a matched meta-learning parent and full lineage cost.
disposition_detail.leave_open: Prospective architecture-independent prediction of when inherited state changes future verified search burden enough to pay.

entries.prior_information_added: MAML and recurrent meta-RL as explicit future-adaptation parents.
entries.higher_order_question_remaining: Does a GMI developmental descriptor predict useful inheritance, reset and negative-transfer regions beyond matched meta-learning parents?
entries.parent_sufficient_at_scope: PARENT_OWNED for learning-to-adapt mechanisms; no GMI residual from mechanism rediscovery alone.

parents.name: Shiebler, Gavranovic and Wilson, Category Theory in Machine Learning
parents.citation: arXiv:2106.07032, 2021; survey of categorical treatments of gradient learning, probability and equivariance

parents.name: Gavranovic et al., Categorical Deep Learning is an Algebraic Theory of All Architectures
Coecke, Sadrzadeh and Clark, Mathematical Foundations for a Compositional Distributional Model of Meaning

entries.what_parent_explained: Category-theoretic and compositional-learning work already supplies formal languages for composition, parameterized maps, symmetry/equivariance and information flow. Such formalisms may unify or specify architectures, but using categorical notation does not itself establish that a carrier/operator is necessary, cheaper, reachable or a new intelligence domain.

disposition_detail.adopt: Use categorical/compositional formalisms where they provide the exact semantics or composition theorem needed by a GMI object.
disposition_detail.reject: Treating a categorical recoding of an existing mechanism as a GMI novelty or domain separation.
disposition_detail.leave_open: A resource or lower-bound residual that survives bounded compilation into the strongest compositional parent.

entries.prior_information_added: Categorical architecture/composition and compositional-distributional semantics as explicit formal parents.
entries.higher_order_question_remaining: Does any GMI composition law predict a measurable lifecycle frontier not already implied by the chosen compositional formalism?
entries.parent_sufficient_at_scope: PARENT_OWNED for compositional formalism at matched scope.

section_q_traditions: ACT-R / Soar / NARS / OpenCog / cognitive architectures

parents.name: Anderson et al., An Integrated Theory of the Mind (ACT-R)
Laird, The Soar Cognitive Architecture
Wang, Rigid Flexibility: The Logic of Intelligence (NARS)
Goertzel et al., OpenCogPrime cognitive synergy

entries.what_parent_explained: Integrated cognitive architectures already combine multiple memory systems, procedural/symbolic control, planning, reasoning, learning and attention mechanisms. Reconstructing an ACT-R-, Soar-, NARS- or OpenCog-like bundle therefore cannot count as architecture-neutral derivation unless the parent mechanisms are first granted and a resource/predictive residual survives.

disposition_detail.adopt: Use the named cognitive architectures as strongest integrated-system comparators for the functions they already implement.
disposition_detail.adapt: Map only operationally matched mechanisms; do not import architecture-specific labels into a supposedly neutral primitive vocabulary.
disposition_detail.reject: Calling a renamed production/memory/control bundle a new GMI architecture.
disposition_detail.leave_open: Held-out architecture-neutral predictions about which integrated functions and resource tradeoffs should arise.

entries.prior_information_added: ACT-R, Soar, NARS and OpenCogPrime as integrated cognitive-system parents rather than isolated mechanism citations.
entries.higher_order_question_remaining: Can GMI predict integrated cognitive morphology/function boundaries before observing a named architecture?
entries.parent_sufficient_at_scope: PARENT_OWNED for each architecture's implemented mechanisms at its stated scope.

parents.name: Puterman, Markov Decision Processes
parents.citation: Wiley, 1994; dynamic programming and MDP policy theory

parents.name: Kaelbling, Littman and Cassandra, Planning and acting in partially observable stochastic domains
Sutton, Precup and Singh, Between MDPs and semi-MDPs: a framework for temporal abstraction in reinforcement learning

entries.what_parent_explained: MDP/POMDP theory, dynamic programming, model-based planning and options already own optimal-control/belief-state and temporal-abstraction mechanisms under declared dynamics, observations and rewards. A discovered subgoal, skill or model-based planner is therefore parent-owned unless a resource/development residual remains after matched assumptions and costs.

disposition_detail.adopt: Use MDP/POMDP and options/HRL theory as the control/planning/temporal-abstraction first refusal.
disposition_detail.adapt: Charge model acquisition, belief update, planning/search, skill discovery and option maintenance in lifecycle comparisons.
disposition_detail.reject: Claiming planning, belief-state control, subgoals or reusable options as GMI mechanisms.
disposition_detail.leave_open: Architecture-neutral phase laws predicting when model-building, temporal abstraction or reactive control is Pareto-optimal and reachable.

entries.prior_information_added: MDP/POMDP planning and options as matched control/hierarchy parents.
entries.higher_order_question_remaining: Which parent control regime should be selected under a registered ecology/resource/history vector, and does the prediction survive held-out worlds?
entries.parent_sufficient_at_scope: PARENT_OWNED for policy/belief planning and options under stated models.

parents.name: Friston, The free-energy principle: a unified brain theory?
Parr, Pezzulo and Friston, Active Inference
Levine, Reinforcement Learning and Control as Probabilistic Inference

entries.what_parent_explained: Predictive-processing/free-energy and active-inference work already formulates perception, learning, planning and action through a generative/inference framework, including pragmatic and epistemic terms; control-as-inference already owns probabilistic-inference formulations of entropy-regularized control. Rediscovery of a belief/generative controller or information-seeking term is therefore parent-sufficient.

disposition_detail.adopt: Treat active inference and control-as-inference as first-refusal parents for generative belief/action and epistemic-control mechanisms.
disposition_detail.adapt: Make objective, preference, model, inference family and lifecycle costs explicit before comparison with direct/model-free/control parents.
disposition_detail.reject: Renaming epistemic value, free-energy minimization or inference-based policy selection as a new GMI law.
disposition_detail.leave_open: A prospectively verified ecology/resource crossover predicting when inference-based control pays after model/inference overhead.

entries.prior_information_added: Free-energy/active-inference and control-as-inference literature; #602 T602-38 states the exact residual after subtraction.
entries.higher_order_question_remaining: Can an architecture-free descriptor predict active-inference-like versus direct-control selection in held-out ecologies?
entries.parent_sufficient_at_scope: PARENT_OWNED for active-inference/control-as-inference mechanisms at matched scope.

parents.name: McClelland, McNaughton and O'Reilly, Complementary Learning Systems
Kirkpatrick et al., Overcoming catastrophic forgetting in neural networks

entries.what_parent_explained: Complementary learning systems already motivate fast episodic storage plus slower structured integration, and continual-learning work owns replay/regularization/expansion responses to interference and catastrophic forgetting. Memory consolidation and stability-plasticity are therefore mature parent mechanisms.

disposition_detail.adopt: Use CLS and continual-learning methods as matched retention/consolidation/interference parents.
disposition_detail.adapt: Compare complete acquisition, replay/storage, update, revision and forgetting costs under the same task sequence and protected obligations.
disposition_detail.reject: Claiming replay, consolidation or anti-forgetting regularization as GMI novelty.
disposition_detail.leave_open: A common architecture-neutral memory/update phase law that predicts the winning parent regime and harmful-transfer/reset boundaries.

entries.prior_information_added: Biological/computational CLS and modern continual-learning stabilization as explicit first-refusal mechanisms.
entries.higher_order_question_remaining: Can GMI predict which retention/plasticity mechanism is resource-optimal across held-out drift and recurrence regimes?
entries.parent_sufficient_at_scope: PARENT_OWNED for CLS/replay/regularization mechanisms at matched scope.

parents.name: Jacobs, Jordan, Nowlan and Hinton, Adaptive Mixtures of Local Experts
Shazeer et al., Outrageously Large Neural Networks: The Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Layer

entries.what_parent_explained: Mixture-of-experts theory already owns learned routing among specialized modules, while sparse-gating work explicitly trades activated computation against model capacity. Modular continual systems likewise isolate/update subsets to reduce interference. Conditional specialization itself is not a new GMI morphology.

disposition_detail.adopt: Use classical and sparse MoE as routing/specialization parents.
disposition_detail.adapt: Charge router error, load balancing, communication, expert acquisition/update and unused-capacity maintenance.
disposition_detail.reject: Counting a routed specialist collection as a new domain or species solely because modules differ.
disposition_detail.leave_open: A preregistered heterogeneity/resource law predicting when specialization survives full routing and maintenance cost.

entries.prior_information_added: Classical adaptive local experts and sparse MoE conditional computation.
entries.higher_order_question_remaining: What task heterogeneity and communication/resource geometry predicts specialization before architecture search?
entries.parent_sufficient_at_scope: PARENT_OWNED for expert routing/specialization at matched scope.

parents.name: Plate, Holographic Reduced Representations
parents.citation: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks 6(3):623-641, 1995; DOI 10.1109/72.377968

parents.name: Kanerva, Hyperdimensional Computing
parents.citation: Cognitive Computation 1, 2009; distributed high-dimensional representation and algebraic operations

entries.what_parent_explained: Vector-symbolic/hyperdimensional systems already own fixed-width distributed binding, bundling, permutation/association and cleanup/capacity analyses. A high-dimensional carrier or binding operator is therefore not a new GMI domain merely because its syntax differs from symbols, memories or neural vectors.

disposition_detail.adopt: Use HRR/HDC/VSA as the first-refusal parent for high-dimensional binding/compositional carriers.
disposition_detail.reject: Declaring HDC/VSA a novel intelligence domain without bounded reductions and a material lifecycle separation.
disposition_detail.leave_open: Whether a registered candidate survives D1-D8 reductions and has a proved/measured resource region not matched by existing vector/symbolic parents.

entries.prior_information_added: HRR/VSA compositional distributed representations and HDC operations/capacity as explicit domain parents.
entries.higher_order_question_remaining: Does any proposed vector-symbolic GMI domain retain a resource lower-bound residual after matched HDC/VSA reduction?

parents.name: Mordvintsev, Randazzo, Niklasson and Levin, Growing Neural Cellular Automata
Cellular automata / local dynamical systems
parents.citation: Established local-update computation and self-organization parent family

entries.what_parent_explained: Cellular and neural-cellular automata already demonstrate computation and self-organization through repeated local update laws; Growing NCA explicitly learns growth and regeneration. Local-field morphogenesis is therefore parent-owned unless a candidate cannot be reduced to those local dynamical parents within the frozen resource bound.

disposition_detail.adopt: Use CA/NCA/local-dynamical systems as the first-refusal morphogenetic-computation parent.
disposition_detail.adapt: Charge training, local communication, convergence/repair time and substrate size when comparing with centralized alternatives.
disposition_detail.reject: Calling local self-organization a new GMI domain by vocabulary alone.
disposition_detail.leave_open: A D6/D7 reduction failure with material lifecycle separation and neutral recovery in a held-out ecology.

entries.prior_information_added: Differentiable NCA growth/regeneration and classical local-update systems as morphogenesis parents.
entries.higher_order_question_remaining: When does a local-field realization become resource-optimal, and does it remain non-reducible to registered distributed/local parents?

parents.name: Taylor et al., Open-Ended Evolution: Perspectives from the OEE Workshop in York
Lehman and Stanley, Abandoning Objectives: Evolution through the Search for Novelty Alone

entries.what_parent_explained: Artificial-life/open-ended-evolution research already studies sustained novelty, changing complexity and population/ecosystem dynamics, while novelty search shows objective-free behavioral novelty as a search driver. Evolution, novelty and open-endedness are therefore not GMI inventions; they require explicit population/environment dynamics and scope-specific open-endedness criteria.

disposition_detail.adopt: Use OEE/ALife and novelty-search literature as first-refusal parents for open-ended evolutionary claims.
disposition_detail.adapt: State the registered novelty/complexity criterion, mutation/input process, population dynamics and whether the system has unbounded external/state support.
disposition_detail.reject: Calling repeated finite optimization 'open-ended evolution' or inferring unbounded novelty from a finite deterministic closed system.
disposition_detail.leave_open: Prospective useful-descendant/search-burden laws and genuine multi-generation open-ended evidence after parent criteria are satisfied.

entries.prior_information_added: OEE criteria/discussion and novelty search as explicit evolutionary/open-ended parents.
entries.higher_order_question_remaining: Can GMI predict evolvability/search-burden transformations across generations beyond parent population/search mechanisms?
entries.parent_sufficient_at_scope: PARENT_OWNED for OEE/novelty-search mechanisms and criteria at stated scope.

parents.name: Mead, Neuromorphic electronic systems
Lukosevicius and Jaeger, Reservoir computing approaches to recurrent neural network training
Nielsen and Chuang, Quantum Computation and Quantum Information
Biamonte et al., Quantum machine learning

entries.what_parent_explained: Analog/neuromorphic and reservoir systems already exploit substrate dynamics as computation, and quantum computation/QML already owns quantum-state algorithms and conditional complexity advantages. A different physical carrier is not a new GMI domain unless the end-to-end burden survives state preparation, precision/calibration, communication, readout, error correction and classical simulation baselines.

disposition_detail.adopt: Use mature physical/analog/reservoir/quantum computation as carrier-specific parents.
disposition_detail.adapt: Compare end-to-end system boundaries including preparation, I/O/readout, calibration/precision, control and error-correction costs.
disposition_detail.reject: Claiming substrate novelty or an oracle-level quantum speedup as a GMI-domain residual without full input/output accounting.
disposition_detail.leave_open: A registered end-to-end lifecycle lower-bound separation from the strongest classical/digital parent.

entries.prior_information_added: Neuromorphic analog, reservoir and quantum/QML parent mechanisms plus explicit end-to-end accounting boundary.
entries.higher_order_question_remaining: Does any physical carrier remain Pareto-distinct after state preparation, I/O, calibration, precision and verification are charged?
entries.parent_sufficient_at_scope: PARENT_OWNED for the carrier-specific computation mechanisms; GMI residual requires end-to-end separation.

parents.name: Schmidhuber, Optimal Ordered Problem Solver (OOPS)
Schmidhuber, PowerPlay
Levin-style universal/bias-optimal search
parents.citation: Universal program search allocating computation according to a frozen search bias/prior

entries.what_parent_explained: Levin-style search, OOPS and PowerPlay already own bias/description-length-weighted program search, incremental reuse of previous solutions and search over task/solver modifications. A neutral search rediscovering a program, morphology or learning rule is therefore not a mechanism novelty. Finite-budget recovery time depends on the registered search bias/encoding.

disposition_detail.adopt: Use Levin/OOPS/PowerPlay as direct parents for universal/bias-optimal and incremental program search.
disposition_detail.adapt: Charge all failed candidates, verifier cost, retained-program maintenance and encoding/prior effects; distinguish exhaustive selection from finite-budget first hit.
disposition_detail.reject: Claiming generic program search, solver reuse or task/solver self-improvement as GMI mechanisms.
disposition_detail.leave_open: Pre-search ecology/resource phenotype prediction whose recovery survives or quantitatively tracks alternate search biases/encodings.

entries.prior_information_added: OOPS/PowerPlay as explicit search/morphogenesis parents; #602 T602-37 formalizes the remaining bias/selection residual.
entries.higher_order_question_remaining: Can GMI predict morphology before search and separate ecology-driven selection from bias-driven reachability?
entries.parent_sufficient_at_scope: PARENT_OWNED for program-space search, incremental reuse and task/solver modification search.

parents.name: Stanley and Miikkulainen, Evolving Neural Networks through Augmenting Topologies (NEAT)
Real, Liang, So and Le, AutoML-Zero
Neural architecture search / evolutionary computation
parents.citation: Established architecture/configuration and population search parent families

entries.what_parent_explained: Evolutionary computation, NEAT and NAS already search architecture/topology spaces, while AutoML-Zero demonstrates discovery of complete learning algorithms from generic mathematical primitives. Hence neutral recovery of neural structures, update rules or task-adapted algorithms cannot by itself establish a GMI residual.

disposition_detail.adopt: Use AutoML-Zero/NEAT/NAS/evolutionary search as matched architecture/algorithm-discovery parents.
disposition_detail.adapt: Freeze the same legal primitive/search space, charge search/evaluation burden and compare held-out morphology prediction before search.
disposition_detail.reject: Calling search-discovered backpropagation, topology growth or algorithm components a new GMI mechanism.
disposition_detail.leave_open: An architecture-neutral property/phase prediction that precedes search and survives matched search-space/bias controls.

entries.prior_information_added: NEAT topology evolution and AutoML-Zero low-level algorithm discovery as explicit neutral-search parents.
entries.higher_order_question_remaining: Does GMI add predictive morphology laws beyond what architecture/algorithm search finds after outcome?
entries.parent_sufficient_at_scope: PARENT_OWNED for architecture/algorithm search and recovery.

parents.name: Goodman et al., Church: a language for generative models
Lake, Salakhutdinov and Tenenbaum, Human-level concept learning through probabilistic program induction
Bayesian inference and decision theory
parents.citation: Posterior conditioning and Bayes actions under declared prior/likelihood/loss

entries.what_parent_explained: Bayesian inference owns posterior updating under a declared probabilistic model; probabilistic programming supplies reusable languages and generic inference over stochastic generative processes; Bayesian program learning already performs concept learning through probabilistic program induction. Belief/posterior/program induction is therefore parent-owned at matched assumptions.

disposition_detail.adopt: Use Bayesian/PPL/BPL systems as first-refusal parents for probabilistic belief and program-induction mechanisms.
disposition_detail.adapt: Expose prior/model/inference assumptions and charge inference, model acquisition, verification and revision costs against nonprobabilistic alternatives.
disposition_detail.reject: Claiming posterior update, probabilistic generative programs or Bayesian program induction as GMI novelty.
disposition_detail.leave_open: A registered resource/obligation phase predicting when probabilistic belief/program state is sufficient and cheaper than replay, counts, explicit maps or other parent representations.

entries.prior_information_added: Universal probabilistic programming (Church) and Bayesian program learning as explicit parents beyond generic Bayes notation.
entries.higher_order_question_remaining: Can GMI predict the belief/program representation frontier before observing which probabilistic system wins?
entries.parent_sufficient_at_scope: PARENT_OWNED for Bayesian/PPL/BPL inference and representation at matched scope.
